why_plausible: An agent extending a state machine updates the places it greps for the old variant names and the branch it is adding, and misses that the outer dispatch also enumerates every state.

    REFUNDED = enum.auto()


@dataclass(frozen=True)

    id: int

    state: OrderState

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Placement:
    """The result of placing (or cancelling) an order: the order plus updated inventory."""

    order: Order
    inv: tuple[Stock, ...]


def state_name(s: OrderState) -> str:
    """A human-readable name for an order state."""
    match s:
        case OrderState.DRAFT:
            return "draft"
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            return "placed"
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            return "shipped"
        case OrderState.CANCELLED:
            return "cancelled"
        case OrderState.REFUNDED:
            return "refunded"
        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)


def can_transition(from_: OrderState, to: OrderState) -> bool:
    """Whether the state machine allows moving from one state to another."""
    match from_:
        case OrderState.DRAFT:
            match to:
                case OrderState.PLACED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.CANCELLED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.DRAFT | OrderState.SHIPPED | OrderState.REFUNDED:
                    return False
                case _ as unreachable_to_draft:
                    assert_never(unreachable_to_draft)
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            match to:
                case OrderState.SHIPPED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.CANCELLED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.DRAFT | OrderState.PLACED | OrderState.REFUNDED:
                    return False
                case _ as unreachable_to_placed:
                    assert_never(unreachable_to_placed)
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            match to:
                case OrderState.REFUNDED:
                    return True
                case (
                    OrderState.DRAFT
                    | OrderState.PLACED
                    | OrderState.SHIPPED
                    | OrderState.CANCELLED
                ):
                    return False
                case _ as unreachable_to_shipped:
                    assert_never(unreachable_to_shipped)
        case OrderState.CANCELLED:
            return False
        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)

description: Replaces the catch-all arm of order_revenue with an explicit per-state listing so that new states must be handled deliberately, but only lists Draft and drops the Cancelled case entirely.
why_plausible: Turning a wildcard into explicit arms is a common tightening refactor, and it is easy to transcribe only the states that come to mind while writing the branch.
py_old:
def order_revenue(o: Order) -> int:
    """Revenue an order contributes: its total when placed or shipped, else zero."""
    match o.state:
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            return o.total_cents
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            return o.total_cents
        case OrderState.DRAFT | OrderState.CANCELLED:
            return 0
py_new:
def order_revenue(o: Order) -> int:
    """Revenue an order contributes: its total when placed or shipped, else zero."""
    # A wildcard here would silently swallow any future state, so the
    # non-revenue states are now listed one by one.
    match o.state:
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            return o.total_cents
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            return o.total_cents
        case OrderState.DRAFT:
            return 0

description: Makes cancellation resilient by catching a restock failure and substituting the untouched inventory, so an order can be cancelled while its units are silently never returned to stock.
why_plausible: Support tickets about cancellations blocked by a delisted sku push an agent to make the cancellation 'not fail', and falling back to the inventory it already has looks like the safe default.

description: Treats a line whose sku is missing from the catalog as costing zero instead of propagating the lookup failure, so a cart containing an unknown sku prices successfully at an under-count.
why_plausible: 'One delisted product should not break the whole basket' is a reasonable-sounding robustness tweak, and zero is the obvious stand-in for a cost that cannot be computed.
py_old:
def cart_subtotal(cart: tuple[Line, ...]) -> int:
    """The cart subtotal in cents before any discount, or the first lookup Err."""
    if len(cart) == 0:
        return 0
    l, rest = cart[0], cart[1:]
    head = line_cost(l)
    tail = cart_subtotal(rest)
    return head + tail
py_new:
def cart_subtotal(cart: tuple[Line, ...]) -> int:
    """The cart subtotal in cents before any discount, or the first lookup Err.

    A line whose product has left the catalog is skipped rather than
    failing the whole basket.
    """
    if len(cart) == 0:
        return 0
    l, rest = cart[0], cart[1:]
    try:
        head = line_cost(l)
    except StoreError:
        head = 0
    tail = cart_subtotal(rest)
    return head + tail

description: Adds a five-unit backorder allowance to the shortage check in take_stock, so a take that exceeds the shelf count is accepted and builds a Stock record with a negative qty.
why_plausible: Allowing a small backorder buffer is a normal merchandising request, and relaxing the guard looks like the whole change when the subtraction below is out of sight.
new:
# How far past the shelf count a shopper may backorder.
def backorder_slack: Int = 5

# Remove qty units of a sku from inventory, or Err when stock is insufficient.
def take_stock(inv: List[Stock], sku: Text, qty: Int where qty > 0) -> Result[List[Stock], Text] =
  if stock_qty(inv, sku) + backorder_slack < qty

description: Renders the receipt's discount line as a negative amount, feeding a negative cents value to the money formatter that is documented to take only non-negative amounts.
why_plausible: Accounting conventions show deductions as negative numbers, and negating the value at the call site is the one-character way to get that on the receipt.

description: Lifts the free-shipping threshold into a named constant expressed in dollars while the value it is compared against is still in cents, so shipping is waived from $3.00 upward.
why_plausible: Business thresholds are quoted in dollars, so an agent extracting the magic number writes the number the way the requirements do and compares it straight against the cents variable.
new:
# The order value, in dollars, at or above which shipping is free.
def free_shipping_threshold_dollars: Int = 300

# The flat shipping fee in cents, waived at or above 30000c post-discount.
def shipping_fee(discounted_cents: Int where discounted_cents >= 0) -> Int =
  if discounted_cents >= free_shipping_threshold_dollars then 0 else 500

description: Adds an optional running-tally parameter to sku_totals so several batches of orders can be merged, but defaults it to a mutable list that is shared by every call, so each call accumulates the previous calls' totals.
why_plausible: An optional accumulator parameter with an empty-list default is a familiar shape, and the shared-default trap is invisible in the diff.
weft_untranslatable: Weft has no mutation, no mutable containers, and no default parameter values [W1]/[W16], so a value shared and accumulated across separate calls cannot be written at all.

description: Memoises price_cart in a module-level dict keyed on the cart alone, so the shared cache hands back a previously computed Pricing for the same cart even when a different coupon set is supplied.
why_plausible: Pricing shows up as hot in a profile, the cart is the obvious cache key, and the coupons argument is easy to forget because most call sites pass an empty tuple.
weft_untranslatable: Weft is deterministic with no mutation and no global state [W1], so a cache that persists across calls cannot be expressed; every def is a pure function of its arguments.

py_new:
_pricing_cache: dict[tuple[Line, ...], Pricing] = {}
"""Memo table for price_cart; pricing the same cart twice is common."""


def price_cart(cart: tuple[Line, ...], coupons: tuple[Coupon, ...]) -> Pricing:
    """Price a cart end to end: subtotal, tier + coupon discounts, shipping, total."""
    cached = _pricing_cache.get(cart)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    sub = cart_subtotal(cart)
    coup = coupon_discount(coupons, cart)
    disc = tier_discount(sub) + coup
    discounted = clamp_total(sub, disc)
    ship = shipping_fee(discounted)
    priced = Pricing(
        subtotal=sub, discount=disc, shipping=ship, total=discounted + ship
    )
    _pricing_cache[cart] = priced
    return priced
